claims.text: A slow thermal ramp during polyol reduction promotes synchronous reduction of Pt, Pd, Rh, Au, and Ru precursors.
Synchronous precursor reduction leads to uniform atomic mixing in Pt–Pd–Rh–Au–Ru nanoparticles.
Synchronous precursor reduction produces a single-phase Pt–Pd–Rh–Au–Ru alloy.
Uniformly mixed, single-phase nanoparticles made using a slow ramp exhibit superior catalytic performance to rapidly heated nanoparticles.
The proposed initial state is a homogeneous solution of Pt, Pd, Rh, Au, and Ru salts in a polyol solvent under an inert atmosphere.
The synthesis is intended to form nanoparticles with sizes of 5–10 nm.
The controlled comparison uses a 1 °C/min ramp to 200 °C versus direct heating to 200 °C.
Synchronized nucleation and growth under controlled thermal conditions produce atomic-scale mixing and phase homogeneity.
A slow thermal ramp causes gradual and nearly simultaneous reduction of the different metal ions.
Rapid heating causes asynchronous reduction of the different metal ions.
Asynchronous reduction results in phase segregation or compositional inhomogeneity.
Phase segregation or compositional inhomogeneity negatively affects catalytic performance.
Slow-ramped nanoparticles will have greater compositional uniformity and less phase segregation than the fast-heated baseline.
Slow-ramped nanoparticles will exhibit lower electrocatalytic overpotential than the fast-heated baseline.
The proposed effect is expected to hold for 5–10 nm Pt–Pd–Rh–Au–Ru nanoparticles produced by polyol reduction under inert conditions.
Surface-energy and kinetic effects are significant for Pt–Pd–Rh–Au–Ru nanoparticles in the 5–10 nm size range.
